sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### M87: IceCube limits neutrino emission during the LHAASO TeV flare

An IceCube follow-up published on **23 November at 07:59 UTC** searched for track-like muon neutrinos from M87 over **14 November 00:00 to 18 November 00:00 UTC**. The result is consistent with atmospheric background, with **p = 1.0**. For an assumed E⁻² spectrum, the **90% confidence upper limit on time-integrated muon-neutrino emission** is **E² dN/dE = 3.9 × 10⁻² GeV cm⁻²**. The central 90% of the expected detected events for that spectrum and declination lie between approximately **930 GeV and 1.5 PeV**. These are fluence units, not a per-second flux. [ATel 18165](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18165).

This follows LHAASO-WCDA's report of enhanced gamma rays on **15–17 November**, with a peak on 16 November. Its preliminary spectrum spans roughly **0.5–20 TeV**, with photon index **1.68 ± 0.29** (statistical uncertainty), an integral flux above 1 TeV around **0.5 Crab**, and a three-day test statistic **TS = 122**, quoted as about 11σ. The announcement does not specify a global trials correction. [ATel 18161](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18161).

The neutrino non-detection constrains emission during the stated four-day window under the spectral assumption; it neither excludes all hadronic models nor demonstrates that M87 emits no neutrinos. A model comparison must match flavor, spectrum and time window rather than directly equating the gamma-ray flux with this fluence bound.

#### IceCube-261123A: a Bronze track candidate with a revised direction

IceCube detected the event at **23 November 06:54:16.99 UTC**. The initial notice was issued at 06:55:04 UTC; revision 1 followed at 08:27:53 UTC. It reports an energy estimator of **145.04 TeV**, signalness **0.45677**, and atmospheric-background false-alarm rate **1.2048 yr⁻¹**. The energy estimate depends on the adopted astrophysical spectrum; signalness is a model-dependent signal/background estimate, not proof of an astrophysical origin or a source association. [Original and revised notices](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/notices_amon_g_b/143530_34667334.amon); [notice-table definitions](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/amon_icecube_gold_bronze_events.html).

The offline reconstruction gives **RA 320.45° (+1.59°/−1.35°), Dec +24.58° (+1.68°/−1.56°)**, J2000, with the quoted coordinate uncertainties describing **90% PSF containment**. The revised legacy notice separately gives a circular statistical-only 90% radius of **88.30 arcmin**; that summary is not interchangeable with the full directional probability map. IceCube reports normal detector operation and no FL16Y gamma-ray catalogue source within the 90% region. No counterpart identification or retraction was present in the checked Circulars through 46346. [GCN 46345](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46345). Catalogue non-coincidence does not exclude an uncatalogued, faint or obscured source. The Swift/BAT targeted-search entry remained pending, not a BAT non-detection. [BAT portal](https://guano.swift.psu.edu/).

#### GRB 261121A: a short pulse with extended emission and distinct spectral intervals

Fermi/GBM and GECAM-B detected this burst on **21 November at approximately 13:23:56.5 UTC**. The GBM direction is **RA 254.7°, Dec +14.7°**, with **6.0° statistical uncertainty**; its supplied HEALPix map includes the estimated localization systematic. [GCN 46326](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46326).

GECAM-B measures **T₉₀ = 0.42 ± 0.02 s** in about **70–6000 keV**. Over T₀−0.2 to T₀+0.4 s, its cutoff-power-law fit gives index **−0.54 (+0.26/−0.21)**, **E_peak = 153 (+67/−38) keV**, and **10–1000 keV fluence 2.56 (+0.22/−0.20) × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²**. [GCN 46333](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46333).

GBM instead reports a bright initial pulse plus extended emission, with **T₉₀ ≈ 52 s** in **50–300 keV**. Its preliminary T₀−0.8 to T₀+51 s fit quotes index **−1.31 ± 0.04**, **E_peak = 3740 ± 40 keV**, fluence **(5.9 ± 0.3) × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²** in 10–1000 keV, and one-second peak photon flux **5.3 ± 0.2 photons cm⁻² s⁻¹**. [GCN 46334](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46334).

The notably different durations and peak energies refer to different instruments and integration intervals; they must not be averaged as independent estimates of one fixed spectrum. The reported E_peak values are reproduced as written, pending final catalogue analysis; neither Circular states a confidence convention for its parameter errors. GCN 46333's position matches 46326 despite an erroneous additional citation to 46328. A short initial pulse alone does not establish a compact-binary merger or a gravitational-wave association.

#### GRB 261122B: an X-ray and fading optical counterpart, with corrected event naming

SVOM/ECLAIRs triggered at **22 November 22:46:55 UTC**, burst identifier **sb26112202**. The best image alert has **SNR 22.45** over **5.10 s in 8–120 keV**, at **RA 3.9375°, Dec −38.8029°**, with a **3.97 arcmin 90% radius** including the stated systematic term. MXT began observing 170 s after the trigger and found an uncatalogued X-ray source. These trigger SNR values are not astrophysical false-alarm probabilities. [GCN 46336](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46336).

**Naming correction:** the event is **GRB 261122B**, as explicitly corrected in [GCN 46339](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46339); it must not be merged with GRB 261122A. VT localized the optical counterpart to **RA 3.97386°, Dec −38.82820°**, with quoted uncertainty **0.50 arcsec**. [GCN 46338](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46338).

NOT confirmed it at **i_AB = 18.33 ± 0.06** at 29.2 minutes, while LCO measured **r_AB = 17.84 ± 0.01** at 9.5 minutes and COLIBRÍ found **r_AB = 20.01 ± 0.03** over 3.26–3.79 hours. [GCNs 46340](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46340), [46341](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46341), [46342](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46342).

The later X-band VT analysis reports a decay proportional to approximately **t⁻⁰·⁶** over 3.4 hours, with **VT_B = 18.11 ± 0.06** and **VT_R = 17.41 ± 0.06** at 356 s. These update the preliminary VHF photometry at nearly the same epoch (18.57 ± 0.02 and 17.51 ± 0.01), rather than demonstrating a physical change between those near-simultaneous measurements. The quoted magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction; passbands and calibrations differ. No redshift was reported in the checked thread. [GCN 46344](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46344).

#### EP261122b: a localized X-ray transient with an optical candidate

Einstein Probe/WXT triggered on **22 November at 09:01:06 UTC**, identifier **01709322835**. Its position has a **3 arcmin 90% radius**, including statistical and systematic uncertainty. Automatic FXT follow-up found an uncatalogued source at **RA 17.8020°, Dec +1.8008°**, J2000, with a **10 arcsec 90% radius**, also including both uncertainty components. [GCN 46343](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46343), reported 23 November.

NOT observations beginning **22 November 19:14:19 UTC**, with midpoint 10.50 h after the trigger, found a source absent from the Legacy Survey at **01h11m12.17s, +01°48′01.9″**, with **z_AB = 21.94 ± 0.17**. The photometry is calibrated to Pan-STARRS and uncorrected for Galactic extinction. The FXT team reports positional consistency. [GCN 46335](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46335), including its 23 November edit.

This remains a candidate optical counterpart: a single detection and positional agreement do not establish fading, redshift or a transient class. The initial EP report deferred further characterization until telemetry arrived and did not quote a flux or duration.

#### EP261122a: an X-ray transient without a detected optical counterpart in deep imaging

EP/WXT triggered at **22 November 06:12:37 UTC**, identifier **01799322834**. FXT localized an uncatalogued X-ray source at **RA 49.3112°, Dec +16.4443°**, J2000, with a **20 arcsec 90% radius**, including statistical and systematic uncertainties. The initial WXT radius was 3 arcmin. [GCN 46331](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46331).

COLIBRÍ obtained 55 minutes of r-band exposure from **08:58:23 to 10:13:19 UTC**, 2.763–4.028 h after the trigger. No new source was detected within the WXT region down to **r_AB > 23.25 at 5σ**, without Galactic-extinction correction. [GCN 46332](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46332). This is a band- and epoch-specific limit, not evidence that no counterpart exists; no redshift, source class or physical explanation for the faintness is established by these reports.

#### GRB 261118A: a materially revised GBM localization

A **20 November 15:44:07 UTC correction** changes the direction of the likely short GRB detected on **18 November at 13:17:49 UTC** (trigger **816700674**). The new on-ground position is **RA 340.4°, Dec −6.4°**, J2000, with **8.6° statistical uncertainty**, significantly different from the earlier automatic location in GCN 46317. The LAT boresight separation is 31°. [GCN 46321](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46321).

Follow-up coverage must be assessed against this revised position and the linked systematic-inclusive HEALPix map. An upper limit obtained around the earlier automatic coordinates cannot automatically be applied to the corrected region. This is a localization correction, not a retraction of the burst.

#### GRB 261119A: the previously unclassified trigger is now a likely short GRB

The GBM team identified **trigger 816807700**, observed on **19 November at 19:01:35.03 UTC**, as **GRB 261119A**, a likely short burst, in a Circular issued **20 November at 21:12:14 UTC**. The refined direction is **RA 14.5°, Dec +33.1°**, J2000, with **13.4° statistical uncertainty** and 80° LAT boresight separation. [GCN 46322](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46322).

This updates the candidate-only classification in the previous edition. The Circular supplies neither a quantitative duration/fluence nor a counterpart association; “likely short” is the team's preliminary classification. The broad localization requires the supplied systematic-inclusive map for counterpart searches.

#### GRB 261119B: ground analysis recovers a burst flagged as unreliable onboard

Fermi/GBM's **19 November 20:06:53.85 UTC** trigger **816811618** was initially flagged as an unreliable location by flight software. In a **20 November 21:12:45 UTC** report, the GBM team identifies it as a GRB, likely long, with ground position **RA 216.6°, Dec +38.1°**, J2000, and **13.9° statistical uncertainty**. Its LAT boresight separation was 22°. [GCN 46323](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46323).

This is a revised astrophysical classification of an existing trigger, not a second event. An unreliable initial localization did not establish that the signal was non-astrophysical. The Circular does not provide a duration, fluence, false-alarm probability or identified counterpart.
